chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

If snow afflicts him, then let him look to the felt of his saddle and perform tayammum from its dust, or from something with him. And if he is in a state where he finds nothing but clay, then there is no harm in performing tayammum from it.

key_terms.الثَّلْجُ: snow that creates difficulty in accessing normal material for tayammum
key_terms.الطِّينَ: clay, permitted here when nothing else is available
key_terms.غُبَارِهِ: its dust, used as the material for tayammum
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression of legal permissibility
key_terms.فَيَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum, the dry ablution
key_terms.لِبْدَ سَرْجِهِ: the felt covering of his saddle, from which dust may be taken

ai.seo_question: Can tayammum be performed with dust from a saddle or with clay when snow prevents access to normal earth?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for tayammum when ordinary earth or dust is not readily available due to snow or difficult conditions. It permits using the dust on the felt of a saddle or, if nothing else is found, even clay, showing facilitation in acts of ritual purity.
